punchline: Earl Woods wrote an entire book about training his son, and Geoff Colvin finds a guide behind most top performers.
thirty_sec: Geoff Colvin studied top performers in different fields and found that none got there alone: someone guided them for years. He argues feedback must come from outside, because we cannot judge our own work objectively. The musician hears the right note in their head, the writer knows what they meant. The book does not measure whether people who failed had coaches too.
